traits: Grey to grey-brown cap, 5 to 25 cm, often with a white bloom when young, rolled margin
Pale, close gills, often forked, up to slightly decurrent
Light grey stem, stout, swollen at the base
White, very thick flesh · strong smell, from floury to rancid
safetyNote: Not recommended: even a small portion can upset the digestion of some people. It is mistaken for the livid pinkgill, which is toxic, and whose gills turn pink.
